title: Printing and Comments
description: Ending lines with endl and \n, chaining with <<, escape sequences, and notes that C++ ignores.

content.value: `cout` never moves to a new line by itself. It prints exactly what you send and stays put, so the next print carries straight on.

steps.note: `Hello, ` is printed, and the line stays open.
`world` carries straight on, on the same line.
`!` is added, then `endl` finishes the line.

content.title: Building one line
content.outro: Four instructions, two lines of output.

content.question: What does this print?
options: `AB` on one line, then `C` on the next
content.explain: No `endl` after `A`, so `B` follows it. `endl` then ends that line, so `C` starts a new one.

content.value: A second way to end a line: put `\n` inside the text, or send `"\n"` on its own. A backslash and `n` together mean "new line".

parts.label: new line
parts.note: Two characters in the code, one line break in the output.

content.title: A new line inside the text

content.caption: Leaving the line open is useful too: in Module 3 you will ask a question and let the user type on the same line.

content.value: The difference is small. `endl` also **flushes**: it pushes everything to the screen straight away. `"\n"` only ends the line, so it is a little faster. Either is fine here.

parts.label: a space
parts.note: The only space in the result comes from here.

content.title: One cout, many pieces
content.caption: Pieces come out in order with nothing added between them. Want a space? Put it inside quotes.
`cout` prints numbers too. Text in quotes prints exactly as written, while `2 + 2` without quotes is maths, worked out first. More in Module 2.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `<<` adds no space. To get `Hi there`, put a space inside one of the quotes.

content.value: Text starts and ends with a double quote, so how do you print one? You **escape** it. A backslash `\` means "treat the next character specially".

items.sub: a double quote, without ending the text
a tab: jumps to the next tab stop

parts.label: a quote
parts.note: Printed as `"`, and the text keeps going.

content.caption: Tabs are handy for lining up labels in columns. You will use one in this module's project.

content.real: A sticky note on a recipe
content.text: The cook reads the recipe and ignores the note. The compiler does the same: a **comment** is a note for humans, skipped completely.

content.caption: `//` starts a note that runs to the end of the line. `/*` and `*/` wrap a note over several lines.

content.value: Putting `//` in front of a real instruction switches it off without deleting it. This is **commenting out**, a quick way to test which line causes a problem. Explain **why** in comments: `// bonus point for a fast answer` beats `// add 1 to score`.
content.title: Two good habits

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: The `A` line is commented out with `//` and the `C` line sits inside `/* */`. Only `B` runs.

practice.question: Use three separate `cout` instructions so the output is exactly one line reading: C++ is fun! Only the last one should end the line.
Print this exactly, quotes included: My teacher said "well done" today.
Print a two line shopping list using a single `cout` with `\n` in the middle: Bread on the first line, Milk on the second. Add a comment above it saying what it is.

quiz.question: What happens if you print with `cout` and never send `endl` or `\n`?
options: C++ adds a new line for you anyway.
The next output carries on along the same line.
quiz.explain: `cout` only moves to a new line when you tell it to, with `endl` or `\n`.

quiz.question: What does this print?  `cout << "Game" << "Over" << endl;`
quiz.explain: `<<` sends the pieces one after another with nothing in between. A space has to be written inside the quotes: `"Game" << " " << "Over"`.

quiz.question: How do you print a double quote inside a piece of text?
options: Use two double quotes in a row.
You cannot print a double quote.
quiz.explain: The backslash tells C++ the next character is part of the text rather than the end of it, so `\"` prints a quote.

quiz.question: What happens to a line starting with `//`?
options: It is printed as a message.
quiz.explain: `//` starts a comment: a note for people reading the code. The compiler skips straight past it.

quiz.question: Which escape sequence starts a new line?
quiz.explain: `\n` is a new line, `\t` is a tab, and `\\` prints a single backslash.
